# Sharing Content

Use [IIIF Content State](https://iiif.io/api/content-state/1.0/) to share a selected view of a work.
A compatible viewer can open the same Canvas from the shared link.

This example uses [The town & pass of Boondi, in Rajpootana](/works/the-town-and-pass-of-boondi-in-rajpootana.html)
from the British India art demo. Its [source Manifest](https://api.dc.library.northwestern.edu/api/v2/works/4bdb5a22-6c7f-498d-8e6e-e49ea9bc4778?as=iiif)
contains one Canvas, labeled “recto.”

## Share a view

Open the work and select **Share** in the viewer. Include the current view in the share options,
then copy the link. Readers who follow it open the work at that view.

## Embed the view in a page

Copy the value of the shared link's `iiif-content` query parameter into the `Viewer` component's
`iiifContent` prop. This example opens the print's recto:

```mdx filename="content/about/boondi-view.mdx"
---
title: A View of Boondi
---

# A View of Boondi

Explore the print from Northwestern University Libraries.

<Viewer iiifContent="" />
```

The encoded value contains this Canvas reference. Both IDs come from the provider's Manifest:

```json
{
  "id": "https://api.dc.library.northwestern.edu/api/v2/file-sets/138a94b0-175a-4152-98c7-df58661ce7d5?as=iiif",
  "type": "Canvas",
  "partOf": [
    {
      "id": "https://api.dc.library.northwestern.edu/api/v2/works/4bdb5a22-6c7f-498d-8e6e-e49ea9bc4778?as=iiif",
      "type": "Manifest"
    }
  ]
}
```

IIIF Content State uses URL-safe Base64 encoding to carry JSON in a link. See the
[encoding specification](https://iiif.io/api/content-state/1.0/#6-content-state-encoding) for details.
